title: How many horses and hens have 55 heads and 150 legs?
description: A farm has fifty five heads and one hundred fifty legs, all from horses and hens. A letter for the horses gives twenty horses and thirty five hens, and a method without letters gives the same answer.
teaching_notes: One idea: let a letter be the horses, write the hens as fifty five take away that letter, and count the legs. Watch for students who forget that a hen has two legs and a horse has four.

video_script.why: The child uses the letter for one animal and the other as the total take away it, as in the cycle puzzle, then repeats the answer without letters.
video_script.substitution: Let h be the horses, hens 55 − h, legs 4h + 2 (55 − h) = 150; then 55 hens would have 110 legs, 40 extra, 40 ÷ 2 = 20 horses.
video_script.anchor: a farm with horses and hens, 55 heads and 150 legs written beside it
video_script.payoff_line: There are twenty horses and thirty five hens

final_answer.spoken: twenty horses and thirty five hens

maths_rules: let h be the horses; hens = 55 − h
without letters: 55 hens have 110 legs; 150 − 110 = 40 extra; each horse adds 2; 40 ÷ 2 = 20
video_script.design: One idea: a letter for the horses gives the hens as fifty five take away that letter, and the legs give the equation. The farm stays on the board and the check is the last step.

narration: <bookmark mark='horses'/>Step two, count the legs. Each horse has four legs, so the horses have four aitch legs.
<bookmark mark='hens'/>Each hen has two legs, so the hens have two times, fifty five take away aitch.
<bookmark mark='total'/>All the legs add up to one hundred fifty.
<bookmark mark='open'/>Step three, open the bracket. Two times fifty five is one hundred ten.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Four aitch take away two aitch is two aitch. Then two aitch plus one hundred ten is one hundred fifty.
<bookmark mark='aitch'/>Take away one hundred ten, and two aitch is forty. Aitch is twenty.

narration: <bookmark mark='hens'/>Step four, try it without letters. If all fifty five animals were hens, there would be one hundred ten legs.
<bookmark mark='extra'/>The real count is forty legs more. Each horse in place of a hen adds two legs.
<bookmark mark='horses'/>Forty divided by two gives twenty horses, the same as before.
<bookmark mark='hens'/>Step five, find the hens and check. Fifty five take away twenty is thirty five hens.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Four times twenty is eighty, and two times thirty five is seventy. Together that is one hundred fifty legs.
